questions.q: What is the synchronous Apex limit on total SOQL queries issued in a single transaction?
questions.explain: The documented synchronous limit is 100 total SOQL queries per transaction (asynchronous contexts get a higher limit of 200).

questions.q: What is the Apex limit on total DML statements issued in a single transaction?
questions.explain: The documented limit is 150 total DML statements issued per transaction, the same in both synchronous and asynchronous contexts.

questions.q: What does Limits.getQueries() return when called inside Apex code?
options: The maximum number of SOQL queries ever allowed
The number of SOQL queries issued so far in the current transaction
The number of records returned by the most recent query
The number of DML statements issued so far
questions.explain: Limits.getQueries() returns how many SOQL queries have been issued so far in the current transaction; Limits.getLimitQueries() returns the maximum allowed.

questions.q: Why does it matter to call Limits.getQueries() right after Test.startTest() rather than before it, when measuring a method's query usage?
options: Test.startTest() gives the following code a fresh governor-limit context, so measuring from that point isolates the count to just the method under test
Limits.getQueries() only works inside startTest()/stopTest() blocks
Calling it before startTest() always returns zero regardless of prior queries
questions.explain: Since startTest() resets to a fresh limit context, measuring immediately after it excludes any queries used by setup code that ran earlier in the test method, isolating the measurement to the code under test.

questions.q: What is the maximum total execution time Salesforce allows for a single Apex transaction?
questions.explain: The documented maximum execution time for each Apex transaction is 10 minutes, the same in both synchronous and asynchronous contexts.
